name: Spike - does a weather plan keep a shortened race's clock
notes: A shortened race with generated weather runs a plan, and both planners set the game's own clock to the plan's multiplier while it plays: PURE Planner calls ac.setWeatherTimeMultiplier with the plan's timemulti on every update (PLAN_MGR_update_Timed in apps/lua/PurePlanner/plan/plan_manager.lua), and Sol Planner does the same with timemultiplier as it loads its preset (setTimeMultiplier in apps/python/sol_planner). So the race store now writes the race's own TIME_MULT into the plan, where it used to write 1 and so put the clock back to real time. Step lengths stay in session time: PURE stretches each duration by the multiplier itself (CONTAINER_adapted_duration in plan.lua) and Sol counts playseconds in real seconds. That is read out of their source and not yet driven, which is what this probe is for. PROCEDURE: install the probe plan with `npm run weather -- plan pure clock` (or `sol clock`), then `npm run race -- spikes/time-multiplier-plan` - and for Sol, change weatherController below to sol2 first, since only one controller runs. It starts at 18:00 and the plan says x48. WHAT HAS TO BE TRUE: a game hour passes every 75 seconds, so the clock reads 20:00 at 2.5 minutes and the sun is down soon after, AND the heavy rain arrives about 3 real minutes in and moves off about 6 minutes in. IF THE CLOCK RUNS IN REAL TIME the planner is not taking the multiplier from the plan. IF THE RAIN ARRIVES FAR LATER than 3 minutes - 48 times later would be two and a half hours - step lengths are being read on the game's clock and have to be divided by the multiplier before they are written. Undo with `npm run weather -- plan remove` afterwards.
